title: fix(codex): first Codex turn fails on a busy host while the app-server starts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the first Codex turn failing on a busy host when discovery times out while the shared app-server is still starting.

## User Impact

A caller abandoning discovery no longer cancels shared startup. Later requests can use the ready server, configured startup budgets are honored, and expired acquisitions release their lease without sending a late RPC. Explicit supervision connections keep their existing connection policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared service owns physical startup; each caller owns its wait and subsequent request budget. Timeout normalization now uses the config owner without repeating harness connection admission. Timeout diagnostics and control observations retain the phase that failed before successful cleanup, while cleanup-originated failures retain their own phase.

The original contributor's work and ancestry are preserved. The correction was independently reviewed, then integrated through the native baseline workflow with frozen main `d4babe8e8ba448bd21bdc4c89de0d223a4353faa`.

## Evidence

- Exact prepared source `9a34692c142c9379a21d4971f12cab23eb73a3cd`: **159 shared-client tests passed**, 92.35s Vitest / 97.64s runner, after a frozen dependency install. This is the suite affected by baseline integration.
- Reviewed correction `8ee81894d4ed3bba3330422504b421f9776d0a98`: **270 request, diagnostic, shared-client and configuration tests passed**, 74.73s Vitest / 79.15s runner. The production changes remain byte-identical in the prepared source. Another **21 registration and command tests passed** on the prior correction; those paths are unchanged by the final fixes.
- Reproduced the original two CI failures and five additional supervision/timeout assertions before fixing their causes. The passing tests cover caller cancellation, late lease release, short and long configured startup budgets, explicit connections, and timeout attribution.
- Independent review found no remaining actionable issue. The only overlapping baseline change is an independently reviewed extraction of the same shared-client test helper sequence. Formatting and diff checks pass.
- The candidate uses Codex **0.162.0**. Its [exact release source](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248) confirms initialization precedes normal dispatch and closing single-client stdio ends the server.

Validation limits: the original author's busy-host before/after runtime proof applies to the original PR revision. No new live Gateway/provider call or full evaluation run was performed. Before baseline integration, local typed lint stopped at the SDK declaration generator's 300s timeout under host I/O pressure; the subsequent type check lacked those declarations. No local lint/type pass is claimed. The current head uses the enforced PR CI gate for broad validation.

### CI disposition

Exact-head [CI run 38867771532](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38867771532) completed with 40 successful jobs, 26 skipped jobs, and one inherited lint failure plus its aggregate gate. The sole root error is `typescript(consistent-return)` in `ui/src/pages/debug/debug-overlay.tsx:115`, fixed on main by [#173976](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173976) (`8425c9a0cf88a08614785703753dea3c92811feb`).

The tested merge `0c185b87b263011369c7009d64b335f491b3e9bb` has baseline `0e687614fd9a8b4bca9dde731e1d34348f07366c` and this exact PR head as its ordered parents. Its debug-overlay input is byte-identical to that baseline (`0ed86224da852044b9b5c81b2b1b71f5ffc83c41`); no UI path changes in the PR merge. The aggregate labels it new because the earlier scheduled-main job passed and selected scope was not compared. Native inherited-failure admission uses the inspected job log and unchanged source inputs; this is not a passing full-CI claim.
